key_insight: SearchOS makes open-domain web search more robust by externalizing search progress into shared state so agents can avoid repetitive failures and keep advancing toward grounded answers.
engineering_relevance: It provides a practical multi-agent control framework for search-intensive LLM systems, improving utilization, coordination, and citation-backed output quality under budget constraints.
method: Reframes information seeking as relational schema completion with grounded citations.
Uses Search-Oriented Context Management (SOCM) to track frontier tasks, evidence graphs, coverage maps, and failure memory.
Adds pipeline-parallel scheduling plus a middleware harness and reusable skills to detect stalls, record evidence, and prevent repeated failed search patterns.
evidence_signal: The system is evaluated on WideSearch and GISA, where it reportedly leads all metrics among the compared single- and multi-agent baselines.
watch_item: The added state management, middleware, and skill infrastructure may increase system complexity and integration overhead in real deployments.
paper_title: SearchOS-V1: Towards Robust Open-Domain Information-Seeking Agent Collaboration
